sanskrit: bhavanaṃ paśya vāruṇyā yad etat sarvakāñcanam yāṃ prāpya suratāṃ prāptāḥ surāḥ surapateḥ sakhe
english: Behold this dwelling of Varuṇa, entirely of gold, friend of the lord of gods — having reached which, the gods attained their pleasures.

sanskrit: etāni hṛtarājyānāṃ daiteyānāṃ sma mātale dīpyamānāni dṛśyante sarvapraharaṇāny uta
english: These, O Mātali, are the blazing weapons of all kinds belonging to the Daityas whose kingdoms were seized — they are still visible here.

sanskrit: akṣayāṇi kilaitāni vivartante sma mātale anubhāvaprayuktāni surair avajitāni ha
english: These are said to be imperishable, O Mātali, kept in motion by the power of their influence, conquered indeed by the gods.

sanskrit: atra rākṣasajātyaś ca bhūtajātyaś ca mātale divyapraharaṇāś cāsan pūrvadaivatanirmitāḥ
english: Here, O Mātali, were divine weapons of the Rākṣasa kind and of the Bhūta kind as well, fashioned in former times by the gods.

sanskrit: agnir eṣa mahārciṣmāñ jāgarti varuṇahrade vaiṣṇavaṃ cakram āviddhaṃ vidhūmena haviṣmatā
english: This fire of great flames keeps watch in Varuṇa's lake, and the discus of Viṣṇu is set whirling here by the smokeless, oblation-bearing fire.

sanskrit: eṣa gāṇḍīmayaś cāpo lokasaṃhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ rakṣyate daivatair nityaṃ yatas tad gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ
english: This bow made of Gāṇḍīva wood, charged with the power to destroy the worlds, is perpetually guarded by the gods — hence it is called the Gāṇḍiva bow.

sanskrit: eṣa kṛtye samutpanne tat tad dhārayate balam sahasraśatasaṃkhyena prāṇena satataṃ dhruvam
english: When occasion arises, this bow steadily bears whatever strength is needed, with the power of hundreds of thousands, constantly and without fail.

sanskrit: aśāsyān api śāsty eṣa rakṣobandhuṣu rājasu sṛṣṭaḥ prathamajo daṇḍo brahmaṇā brahmavādinā
english: This, the first-born rod of punishment, created by Brahmā the knower of Brahman even for chastising those kings who befriend Rākṣasas, punishes even those who would otherwise be unchastisable.

sanskrit: etac chatraṃ narendrāṇāṃ mahac chakreṇa bhāṣitam putrāḥ salilarājasya dhārayanti mahodayam
english: This great royal umbrella, proclaimed by the great discus, is held aloft by the sons of Varuṇa, the king of waters, in its full magnificence.

sanskrit: etat salilarājasya chatraṃ chatragṛhe sthitam sarvataḥ salilaṃ śītaṃ jīmūta iva varṣati
english: This umbrella of the king of waters stands in its canopy-hall and pours cool water on all sides like a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: etac chatrāt paribhraṣṭaṃ salilaṃ somanirmalam tamasā mūrchitaṃ yāti yena nārchati darśanam
english: Water dripping from this umbrella, pure as soma, falls into darkness and becomes invisible — one cannot discern it with sight.

sanskrit: bahūny adbhutarūpāṇi draṣṭavyānīha mātale tava kāryoparodhas tu tasmād gacchāva māciram
english: Many wonders of marvellous form remain to be seen here, O Mātali, yet your task stands interrupted — therefore let us go without delay.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca etat tu nāgalokasya nābhisthāne sthitaṃ puram pātālam iti vikhyātaṃ daityadānavasevitam
english: Nārada said: This city situated at the navel of the realm of the Nāgas is known as Pātāla, frequented by Daityas and Dānavas.

sanskrit: idam adbhiḥ samaṃ prāptā ye ke cid dhruvajaṅgamāḥ praviśanto mahānādaṃ nadanti bhayapīḍitāḥ
english: All beings, stationary and moving alike, that reach here along with the waters cry out a great cry as they enter, tormented by fear.

sanskrit: atrāsuro 'gniḥ satataṃ dīpyate vāribhojanaḥ vyāpāreṇa dhṛtātmānaṃ nibaddhaṃ samabudhyata
english: Here an Asuric fire ever blazes, feeding on water; it knew itself to be bound and restrained in its activity.

sanskrit: atrāmṛtaṃ suraiḥ pītvā nihitaṃ nihatāribhiḥ ataḥ somasya hāniś ca vṛddhiś caiva pradṛśyate
english: Here the gods, after drinking the nectar and vanquishing their foes, deposited what remained; from this the waning and waxing of Soma is observed.

sanskrit: atra divyaṃ hayaśiraḥ kāle parvaṇi parvaṇi uttiṣṭhati suvarṇābhaṃ vārbhir āpūrayañ jagat
english: Here a divine horse-head rises at each sacred lunar occasion, golden in brilliance, filling the world with waters.

sanskrit: yasmād atra samagrās tāḥ patanti jalamūrtayaḥ tasmāt pātālam ity etat khyāyate puram uttamam
english: Because all those forms of water fall down here, this excellent city is therefore celebrated as Pātāla.

sanskrit: airāvato 'smāt salilaṃ gṛhītvā jagato hitaḥ megheṣv āmuñcate śītaṃ yan mahendraḥ pravarṣati
english: Airāvata, for the benefit of the world, draws water from here and releases cool water into the clouds, which the great Indra then rains down.

sanskrit: atra nānāvidhākārās timayo naikarūpiṇaḥ apsu somaprabhāṃ pītvā vasanti jalacāriṇaḥ
english: Here dwell aquatic creatures of various forms, sea monsters of many shapes, drinking the soma-bright waters, moving through the deep.

sanskrit: atra sūryāṃśubhir bhinnāḥ pātālatalam āśritāḥ mṛtā divasataḥ sūta punar jīvanti te niśi
english: Here those who have taken refuge in the floor of Pātāla, struck by the rays of the sun, die by day, O charioteer, and come back to life at night.

sanskrit: udaye nityaśaś cātra candramā raśmibhir vṛtaḥ amṛtaṃ spṛśya saṃsparśāt saṃjīvayati dehinaḥ
english: Here at every rising the moon, wreathed in rays, touches the nectar and by that touch revives all embodied beings.

sanskrit: atra te 'dharmaniratā baddhāḥ kālena pīḍitāḥ daiteyā nivasanti sma vāsavena hṛtaśriyaḥ
english: Here dwell those Daityas devoted to unrighteousness, bound and oppressed by Time, their glory stripped away by Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: atra bhūtapatir nāma sarvabhūtamaheśvaraḥ bhūtaye sarvabhūtānām acarat tapa uttamam
english: Here the Lord of Beings, the great lord of all creatures called Bhūtapati, performed the highest austerities for the welfare of all living things.

sanskrit: atra govratino viprāḥ svādhyāyāmnāyakarśitāḥ tyaktaprāṇā jitasvargā nivasanti maharṣayaḥ
english: Here great seers who have taken the vow of the cow, emaciated by self-study and Vedic recitation, who have abandoned their vital breath and won heaven, continue to dwell.

sanskrit: yatratatraśayo nityaṃ yenakenacidāśitaḥ yenakenacidācchannaḥ sa govrata ihocyate
english: He who sleeps wherever and on whatever, eats whatever comes, and covers himself with whatever is at hand — such a one is called a follower of the cow-vow here.

sanskrit: airāvato nāgarājo vāmanaḥ kumudo 'ñjanaḥ prasūtāḥ supratīkasya vaṃśe vāraṇasattamāḥ
english: Airāvata the king of elephants, Vāmana, Kumuda, and Añjana — the finest of elephants — were born in the lineage of Supratīka.

sanskrit: paśya yady atra te kaś cid rocate guṇato varaḥ varayiṣyāva taṃ gatvā yatnam āsthāya mātale
english: Look, O Mātali, if any one of these pleases you as a worthy match on account of his virtues — let us go and make the effort to choose him.

sanskrit: aṇḍam etaj jale nyastaṃ dīpyamānam iva śriyā ā prajānāṃ nisargād vai nodbhidyati na sarpati
english: This egg, placed in the water, blazing as if with splendour, has not burst open nor moved from the very nature of living creatures.

sanskrit: nāsya jātiṃ nisargaṃ vā kathyamānaṃ śṛṇomi vai pitaraṃ mātaraṃ vāpi nāsya jānāti kaś cana
english: I do not hear its origin or nature spoken of, and no one knows its father or mother either.

sanskrit: ataḥ kila mahān agnir antakāle samutthitaḥ dhakṣyate mātale sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram
english: From this, it is said, a great fire will arise at the end of time and will burn up all three worlds, the moving and the unmoving, O Mātali.

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca mātalis tv abravīc chrutvā nāradasyātha bhāṣitam na me 'tra rocate kaś cid anyato vraja māciram
english: Kaṇva said: Then Mātali, having heard Nārada's words, spoke: "None here pleases me — let us go elsewhere without delay."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca hiraṇyapuram ity etat khyātaṃ puravaraṃ mahat daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca māyāśatavicāriṇām
english: Nārada said: This great and excellent city is known as Hiraṇyapura, the city of the Daityas and Dānavas who wander through hundreds of illusions.

sanskrit: analpena prayatnena nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā mayena manasā sṛṭaṃ pātālatalam āśritam
english: Built with no small effort by Viśvakarmā, created by Maya through thought alone, it rests on the floor of Pātāla.

sanskrit: atra māyāsahasrāṇi vikurvāṇā mahaujasaḥ dānavā nivasanti sma śūrā dattavarāḥ purā
english: Here dwell mighty Dānavas of great energy, transforming themselves through thousands of illusions, heroes who were formerly given boons.

sanskrit: naite śakreṇa nānyena varuṇena yamena vā śakyante vaśam ānetuṃ tathaiva dhanadena ca
english: These cannot be brought under control by Śakra, nor by anyone else — not by Varuṇa, not by Yama, and not by Dhanada (Kubera).

sanskrit: asurāḥ kālakhañjāś ca tathā viṣṇupadodbhavāḥ nairṛtā yātudhānāś ca brahmavedodbhavāś ca ye
english: Asuras, Kālakhañjas, those born of Viṣṇu's footstep, Nairṛtas, Yātudhānas, and those born of the Vedic knowledge of Brahmā —

sanskrit: daṃṣṭriṇo bhīmarūpāś ca nivasanty ātmarakṣiṇaḥ māyāvīryopasaṃpannā nivasanty ātmarakṣiṇaḥ
english: — the fanged and terrible-formed, self-protecting ones who possess the power of illusion — they all dwell here protecting themselves.

sanskrit: nivātakavacā nāma dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ jānāsi ca yathā śakro naitāñ śaknoti bādhitum
english: The Dānavas named Nivātakavacas, battle-maddened, — as you know, even Śakra is unable to overpower them.

sanskrit: bahuśo mātale tvaṃ ca tava putraś ca gomukhaḥ nirbhagno devarājaś ca sahaputraḥ śacīpatiḥ
english: Many times, O Mātali, you yourself, your son Gomukha, the king of gods Śacī's lord together with his sons — all were disgraced by them.

sanskrit: paśya veśmāni raukmāṇi mātale rājatāni ca karmaṇā vidhiyuktena yuktāny upagatāni ca
english: Behold, O Mātali, mansions of gold and silver, properly fashioned by skilled workmanship and well arranged.

sanskrit: vaiḍūryaharitānīva pravālarucirāṇi ca arkasphaṭikaśubhrāṇi vajrasārojjvalāni ca
english: Some green as beryl, some radiant as coral, some white as crystal in sunlight, and some ablaze with the essence of diamonds.

sanskrit: pārthivānīva cābhānti punar nagamayāni ca śailānīva ca dṛśyante tārakāṇīva cāpy uta
english: Some shine like earthen structures, others appear to be of mountains; some look like rocky crags, and some resemble stars.

sanskrit: sūryarūpāṇi cābhānti dīptāgnisadṛśāni ca maṇijālavicitrāṇi prāṃśūni nibiḍāni ca
english: Some gleam with the form of the sun, some resemble blazing fire, some are variegated with nets of gems — tall and densely packed.

sanskrit: naitāni śakyaṃ nirdeṣṭuṃ rūpato dravyatas tathā guṇataś caiva siddhāni pramāṇaguṇavanti ca
english: These cannot be fully described in terms of appearance, substance, or quality — they are perfected in every respect and endowed with all measures of excellence.

sanskrit: ākrīḍān paśya daityānāṃ tathaiva śayanāny uta ratnavanti mahārhāṇi bhājanāny āsanāni ca
english: Behold the playgrounds of the Daityas, and their sleeping quarters as well — vessels set with jewels of great worth, and seats.

sanskrit: jaladābhāṃs tathā śailāṃs toyaprasravaṇānvitān kāmapuṣpaphalāṃś caiva pādapān kāmacāriṇaḥ
english: Behold hills resembling rain-clouds, furnished with streams of water, and trees bearing flowers and fruits of desire, moving at will.

sanskrit: mātale kaś cid atrāpi rucitas te varo bhavet atha vānyāṃ diśaṃ bhūmer gacchāva yadi manyase
english: O Mātali, might any eligible match here please you? Or if you think fit, let us go to another region of the earth.

sanskrit: kaṇva uvāca mātalis tv abravīd enaṃ bhāṣamāṇaṃ tathāvidham devarṣe naiva me kāryaṃ vipriyaṃ tridivaukasām
english: Kaṇva said: Mātali then spoke to him who was speaking thus: "O divine sage, I must not do what is displeasing to the dwellers of heaven."

sanskrit: nityānuṣaktavairā hi bhrātaro devadānavāḥ aripakṣeṇa saṃbandhaṃ rocayiṣyāmy ahaṃ katham
english: "For the gods and Dānavas are brothers in perpetual enmity — how can I approve of an alliance with the enemy's side?"

sanskrit: anyatra sādhu gacchāvo draṣṭuṃ nārhāmi dānavān jānāmi tu tathātmānaṃ ditsātmakamalaṃ yathā
english: "Let us wisely go elsewhere — I cannot look upon Dānavas. Yet I know myself as one who is of a giving nature, like a lotus that offers itself."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca ayaṃ lokaḥ suparṇānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ pannagāśinām vikrame gamane bhāre naiṣām asti pariśramaḥ
english: Nārada said: This is the world of the Suparṇas, the birds that feed on serpents — in valour, in flight, and in the bearing of loads, they know no fatigue.

sanskrit: vainateyasutaiḥ sūta ṣaḍbhis tatam idaṃ kulam sumukhena sunāmnā ca sunetreṇa suvarcasā
english: O charioteer, this lineage is spread by six sons of Vainateyī — Sumukha, Sunāman, Sunetra, and Suvarcas —

sanskrit: surūpapakṣirājena subalena ca mātale vardhitāni prasūtyā vai vinatākulakartṛbhiḥ
english: — and by Surūpa the king of birds, and by Subala, O Mātali — grown and multiplied in birth by the founders of Vinatā's lineage.

sanskrit: pakṣirājābhijātyānāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca kaśyapasya tato vaṃśe jātair bhūtivivardhanaiḥ
english: Hundreds of thousands of those born of royal bird descent, born in the lineage of Kaśyapa — those increasers of living beings —

sanskrit: sarve hy ete śriyā yuktāḥ sarve śrīvatsalakṣaṇāḥ sarve śriyam abhīpsanto dhārayanti balāny uta
english: — all of them endowed with prosperity, all bearing the mark of Śrīvatsa, all desiring glory, they bear great strength.

sanskrit: karmaṇā kṣatriyāś caite nirghṛṇā bhogibhojinaḥ jñātisaṃkṣayakartṛtvād brāhmaṇyaṃ na labhanti vai
english: By their actions they are Kṣatriyas — pitiless, eaters of those who enjoy — and because they cause destruction of their kin, they do not attain Brahminhood.

sanskrit: nāmāni caiṣāṃ vakṣyāmi yathā prādhānyataḥ śṛṇu mātale ślāghyam etad dhi kulaṃ viṣṇuparigraham
english: I will tell their names in order of their distinction — listen, O Mātali; this lineage is praiseworthy, being under the protection of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: daivataṃ viṣṇur eteṣāṃ viṣṇur eva parāyaṇam hṛdi caiṣāṃ sadā viṣṇur viṣṇur eva gatiḥ sadā
english: Viṣṇu is the deity of these, Viṣṇu alone is their highest refuge; Viṣṇu ever dwells in their hearts, and Viṣṇu alone is ever their goal.

sanskrit: suvarṇacūḍo nāgāśī dāruṇaś caṇḍatuṇḍakaḥ analaś cānilaś caiva viśālākṣo 'tha kuṇḍalī
english: Suvarṇacūḍa, Nāgāśī, Dāruṇa, Caṇḍatuṇḍaka, Anala, Anila, Viśālākṣa, and Kuṇḍalī —

sanskrit: kāśyapir dhvajaviṣkambho vainateyo 'tha vāmanaḥ vātavego diśācakṣur nimeṣo nimiṣas tathā
english: — Kāśyapi, Dhvajaviṣkambha, Vainateya, Vāmana, Vātavega, Diśācakṣu, Nimeṣa, and likewise Nimiṣa —

sanskrit: trivāraḥ saptavāraś ca vālmīkir dvīpakas tathā daityadvīpaḥ sariddvīpaḥ sārasaḥ padmakesaraḥ
english: — Trivāra, Saptavāra, Vālmīki, Dvīpaka, Daityadvīpa, Sariddvīpa, Sārasa, and Padmakesara —

sanskrit: sumukhaḥ sukhaketuś ca citrabarhas tathānaghaḥ meghakṛt kumudo dakṣaḥ sarpāntaḥ somabhojanaḥ
english: — Sumukha, Sukhaketu, Citrabarhis, Anagha, Meghakṛt, Kumuda, Dakṣa, Sarpānta, and Somabhojana —

sanskrit: gurubhāraḥ kapotaś ca sūryanetraś cirāntakaḥ viṣṇudhanvā kumāraś ca paribarho haris tathā
english: — Gurubhāra, Kapota, Sūryanetra, Cirāntaka, Viṣṇudhanvā, Kumāra, Paribarha, and Hari —

sanskrit: susvaro madhuparkaś ca hemavarṇas tathaiva ca malayo mātariśvā ca niśākaradivākarau
english: — Susvara, Madhuparka, Hemavarṇa, Malaya, Mātariśvā, and the pair Niśākara and Divākara —

sanskrit: ete pradeśamātreṇa mayoktā garuḍātmajāḥ prādhānyato 'tha yaśasā kīrtitāḥ prāṇataś ca te
english: These sons of Garuḍa have been named by me only partially — they have been celebrated in order of their pre-eminence, fame, and vitality.

sanskrit: yady atra na ruciḥ kā cid ehi gacchāva mātale taṃ nayiṣyāmi deśaṃ tvāṃ ruciṃ yatropalapsyase
english: If none here pleases you, come, let us go, O Mātali — I will take you to that region where you will find what you desire.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca idaṃ rasātalaṃ nāma saptamaṃ pṛthivītalam yatrāste surabhir mātā gavām amṛtasaṃbhavā
english: Nārada said: This is the seventh subterranean level named Rasātala, where dwells Surabhī, the mother of cows, born of nectar.

sanskrit: kṣarantī satataṃ kṣīraṃ pṛthivīsārasaṃbhavam ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ sāreṇa rasam ekam anuttamam
english: Perpetually flowing with milk born of the earth's essence — with the essence of the six tastes she yields one unsurpassable flavour.

sanskrit: amṛtenābhitṛptasya sāram udgirataḥ purā pitāmahasya vadanād udatiṣṭhad aninditā
english: She who is blameless arose in ancient times from the mouth of Pitāmaha (Brahmā) as he, thoroughly satisfied with nectar, breathed out the essence.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ kṣīrasya dhārāyā nipatantyā mahītale hradaḥ kṛtaḥ kṣīranidhiḥ pavitraṃ param uttamam
english: From the stream of her milk falling upon the surface of the earth, a lake was formed — a treasury of milk, supremely pure and excellent.

sanskrit: puṣpitasyeva phenasya paryantam anuveṣṭitam pibanto nivasanty atra phenapā munisattamāḥ
english: Surrounding it as if by blossoming foam all around, the foremost sages called Phenapas dwell here, drinking from it.

sanskrit: phenapā nāma nāmnā te phenāhārāś ca mātale ugre tapasi vartante yeṣāṃ bibhyati devatāḥ
english: Named Phenapas, subsisting on foam, O Mātali, they are engaged in fierce austerities — even the gods fear them.

sanskrit: asyāś catasro dhenvo 'nyā dikṣu sarvāsu mātale nivasanti diśāpālyo dhārayantyo diśaḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Four other cows born of her, O Mātali, dwell in all the directions — they are known as the guardian-cows that support the quarters.

sanskrit: pūrvāṃ diśaṃ dhārayate surūpā nāma saurabhī dakṣiṇāṃ haṃsakā nāma dhārayaty aparāṃ diśam
english: Surūpā, daughter of Surabhī, upholds the eastern quarter; Haṃsakā upholds the southern quarter and also the western.

sanskrit: paścimā vāruṇī dik ca dhāryate vai subhadrayā mahānubhāvayā nityaṃ mātale viśvarūpayā
english: The western, Vāruṇī quarter is upheld by the ever great-souled, all-formed Subhadrā, O Mātali.

sanskrit: sarvakāmadughā nāma dhenur dhārayate diśam uttarāṃ mātale dharmyāṃ tathailavilasaṃjñitām
english: A cow named Sarvakāmadughā upholds the northern quarter, O Mātali — the righteous one also known by the name Eilavila.

sanskrit: āsāṃ tu payasā miśraṃ payo nirmathya sāgare manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā devair asurasaṃhitaiḥ
english: The gods together with the Asuras, using Mount Mandara as the churning rod, churned the ocean along with the milk of these cows —

sanskrit: uddhṛtā vāruṇī lakṣmīr amṛtaṃ cāpi mātale uccaiḥśravāś cāśvarājo maṇiratnaṃ ca kaustubham
english: — and drew forth Vāruṇī, Lakṣmī, nectar, the horse-king Uccaiḥśravas, and the jewel-gem Kaustubha, O Mātali.

sanskrit: sudhāhāreṣu ca sudhāṃ svadhābhojiṣu ca svadhām amṛtaṃ cāmṛtāśeṣu surabhiḥ kṣarate payaḥ
english: To those who feed on sudhā she yields sudhā, to those who eat svadhā she yields svadhā, and to those who drink nectar she flows with milk — such is Surabhī.
